newsitem.title: USA: LIPA pact to cut Long Island power rates 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: LIPA pact to cut Long Island power rates 20 pct.

text.p: An agreement by Long Island Lighting Co and Brooklyn Union Gas to sell some assets to the Long Island Power Authority will cut electric rates for Long Island residents by more than 20 percent over the next five years, New York state officials said Wednesday.
A statement issued by the office of Gov. George Pataki said the reduction will start with an immediate rate cut of 18 percent in Nassau County and more than 16 percent in Suffolk County.
Additionally, each ratepayer in Nassau County and Rockaway will receive a $232 cash refund, while those in Suffolk County will receive approximately $100 as part of the agreement.
"This agreement delivers exactly what we need to cut the outrageously excessive electric bills that all Long Islanders have been forced to pay for too long," Pataki said.
He added that the rate cut will allow the area's economy to grow and create new jobs for years to come.

Under the agreement, LIPA will immediately acquire LILCO's retail electric operations, substantially all of its regulatory assets and its 18 percent stake in Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear plant by paying cash for stock valued at about $2.5 billion in a holding company to be formed by Brooklyn Union and LILCO.
The agreement also calls for LIP to assume LILCO's right regarding litigation involving the Shoreham nuclear power plant.
LIPA chaimran Frank Zarb said he would ask the LIPA board to review the agreement at its next meeting on March 21 and send it to the Internal Revenue Service for a formal tax ruling.
Public hearings will be scheduled in both counties to hear residents' views on the agreement, Zarb said.
